documents.title: Neurology Follow-up
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE NEUROLOGY - FOLLOW-UP
Visit 01/21/2025, received 01/24/2025.

Mr. Thayer returns six months after starting carbidopa-levodopa 25/100 TID, with his wife. He tolerates it without nausea. The rest tremor is somewhat less, but he and his wife feel his walking and overall slowness are only partly improved.

Current medications: carbidopa-levodopa 25/100 TID; amlodipine 5 mg daily; docusate 100 mg BID; PEG 3350 PRN.
Allergies: sulfa (rash); latex.

Exam: hypomimia, hypophonia, bradykinesia and rigidity persist, a little less than at the first visit. Gait slow with shortened stride.
MRI brain from August reviewed: age-related atrophy, no focal lesion.

Impression: Parkinson disease, partial response to levodopa.
Plan: add ropinirole, starting low and increasing weekly by our printed schedule to a target of 3 mg three times daily over about two months. Continue carbidopa-levodopa 25/100 TID. Reviewed sleepiness and impulse-control effects to watch for. Call us with any problems; follow up as scheduled.

documents.title: Primary Care Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Routine HTN f/u. Neurology added ropinirole in January; he finished the titration last week and is now on 3 mg three times a day plus the carbidopa-levodopa. Wife says he is moving a little easier in the mornings. No daytime dozing that either of them has noticed. Bowels unchanged on docusate + PEG.
BP fine today. Exam: soft voice, rest tremor R hand, slow but steady gait without a device. Heart and lungs normal. No edema.
A/P: HTN controlled - amlodipine 5 unchanged. Parkinson disease - per neurology, med list updated with ropinirole 3 mg TID. Constipation stable. CMP today. Back in 6 months for the wellness visit.

documents.title: Medicare Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Subsequent AWV, 72 y/o. Daughter with him.
Interval: no ED visits or hospital stays. Parkinson meds unchanged since spring - carbidopa-levodopa 25/100 TID, ropinirole 3 mg TID. Still independent with self-care, a bit slower dressing. Stopped driving at night on his own. No falls.
PHQ-2 0. Cognitive screen: recall 3/3, clock normal.
Home: one level, grab bar in the shower already.
Meds reconciled with the bottles he brought.

Exam: BP at goal. Masked face, quiet voice, rest tremor R hand, cogwheeling at the wrists, slow stooped gait. Heart regular, lungs clear, no edema.

Plan:
- HTN: continue amlodipine 5 mg.
- Parkinson disease: followed by neurology, no changes from me.
- Constipation: stable, continue.
- Labs today: CMP, CBC, lipids, A1c.
- High-dose flu and COVID vaccine given.
- Colonoscopy due 2028. Health care proxy (wife) form scanned.

documents.title: Neurology Follow-up
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE NEUROLOGY - FOLLOW-UP
Visit 08/11/2026, received 08/13/2026.

Mr. Thayer, 72, with Parkinson disease, hypertension and BPH, is seen with his wife, roughly two years after his first visit here for tremor and freezing of gait. Daily tasks are getting harder for him. Since about 2023 he has grown progressively stiffer in his arms and legs, slower in all movement, and more shuffling when he walks. He continues to have a poor sense of smell and constipation, and he now has trouble getting to sleep at night. His wife describes his expression as often blank, and says he can take several seconds before answering a question. No recent head injury.
On direct questioning his wife reports that for about two months he has been seeing people in the house who are not there, mostly in the evening. He knows they are not real and is not frightened by them. No false beliefs or paranoia.

Medications: carbidopa-levodopa 25/100 TID; ropinirole 3 mg TID; amlodipine 5 mg daily; docusate 100 mg BID; PEG 3350 17 g daily PRN.
Allergies: sulfa (rash); latex.
Family history: father Parkinson disease (onset 72); mother Alzheimer disease (onset 75); older brother essential tremor.
Social: never smoker, no alcohol.

Exam: right hand rest tremor that dampens with action; cogwheel rigidity in both upper limbs; bradykinesia; stooped gait with reduced arm swing. Cognitive testing shows slowed processing speed; fully oriented.
Prior MRI brain (08/2024) reviewed: age-appropriate atrophy, no focal lesion.

Impression:
1. Parkinson disease, progressing.
2. Parkinson disease psychosis - well-formed visual hallucinations with insight retained.
3. Sleep-onset insomnia.

Plan:
- Start quetiapine 25 mg at bedtime.
- Continue carbidopa-levodopa 25/100 TID and ropinirole 3 mg TID.
- Return in about 3 months; call sooner if the hallucinations change or he becomes confused.

Neurology
